Note::remove_emojis¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_emojis() const

Delete Emoji Characters From Every Cell¶

remove_emojis() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with emoji characters removed from each cell. Use it to clean user-generated text — social posts, chat logs, reviews — before language processing or display in a context that cannot render emoji.

Unlike the ASCII character-class filters, this one is Unicode-aware: it decodes each character and drops it only if its code point is in an emoji range. Ordinary text, including accented and non-Latin letters, is kept exactly. Nothing is trimmed or collapsed, so removing an emoji from the middle of a sentence can leave a double space.

remove_emojis is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. A cell that is entirely emoji reduces to "".

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"ship it 🚀 today 🎉", "plain text", "👍👍👍"}).remove_emojis())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["ship it  today ", "plain text", ""]

The emoji are gone; the spaces around them remain, and "👍👍👍" becomes empty.

See Also¶

  • Note::keep_ascii: a blunter clean — drop all non-ASCII, not just emoji.

  • Note::NlpAccessor::clean: a broader user-text cleanup pass.

  • Note::strip / pluss::coden::Note::collapse_whitespace: tidy the spacing left behind.
